I ended up letting him go, but he posted photos the following day on his Facebook page stating the job was completed, which is fraudulent advertising, and he did not get my permission to post photos of my house he took on private property. I'm in the process of requesting him to take down those photos. If you're looking for a qualified handyman, I'd look elsewhere.
Edit: The contractor denies ever posting photos of my unfinished project, which violates Section 512(c) of the DMCA. He has since removed the photos but has now stated I still owe him for further labor, materials, and services that remain unpaid. I have all the receipts for the paid labor and materials, so I have no idea what he is referring to. Like I've stated before, if you're looking for a reputable contractor, look elsewhere. The owner is very unprofessional, to say the least. The only reason there are so many 5-Star ratings for this business is that he'll give you a discount if you give him a good review on Google Maps.

author: Colton Smith
text:
He came out and spoke with my wife regarding installing porch railing on our home and we felt great about the work that he was going to do. Although he didn’t seem to understand it was just railing on the front porch, we were still very excited to get it done! About a week later I texted him to check in and see if or what he’d figured the job would cost and maybe a general timeframe.

At that point, he told me that he needs to pass on the job, as he does not “bid against other companies”. We have a residential home that simply needed front porch railing, I’m not gathering bids from a bunch of big companies that are super eager to get my business 😂 I guess I was just supposed to let him do the work at some point and pay whatever he wants at the end without having any idea of what to expect to pay in the first place.

Definitely did not seem like a professional reaction or a very good business decision. Maybe wants to charge way more? No idea. Would’ve like to have used him but I guess we won’t use him or recommend him to anyone. Can’t speak to the quality of his work, though.
